title: Elements and Reactions
summary: Defines the seven standard elements, special powers, aura rules and the asymmetric reaction matrix that can alter enemies, terrain and positioning.

headings.text: How to Avoid a Dominant Reaction

blocks.text: The elemental system of Symphony of Justice is divided into three distinct categories:
STANDARD ELEMENTS → PURE POWERS → UNIQUE POWERS / NON-ELEMENTAL DAMAGE
This distinction is important because not every power follows the same reaction rules.
These are the elements that form the main Reaction Matrix.

Historical documentation uses names such as Water/Aqua, Fire/Fyred, Ice/Icced, Electro/Thunther, Plant/Planted, Wind/Vuelum, and Earth/Terrant interchangeably. The inherited codes can remain as internal identifiers, while player-facing names should be standardized according to the final language of the game.
Pure Powers do not behave as an eighth, ninth, or tenth conventional element. They are specifically designed to alter how the standard elements function. They are:
Represents darkness, weakening, degradation, and exposure.
Its primary historical function is to reduce the enemy's resistance to the element with which Chaos interacts.
Represents amplification, clarity, blessing, and empowerment.
Its primary function is to increase the effectiveness or damage of the element with which it interacts.
Represents elemental condensation, storage, and reproduction.
Its historical function is to capture an element inside a Spectrum sphere or concentration and later release it as area elemental damage.
Its primary function is to take an applied element and convert it into persistent elemental damage associated with Seals.
Time Clock is separate from the conventional elemental system.
It does not generate standard reactions.
Its power comes from manipulating time, enabling concepts such as:
The original documentation specifically establishes that Time Clock gives up elemental reactions in exchange for greater mechanical freedom.
Time Clock does not compete through reactions. It competes through mechanics that conventional elements cannot perform.
abilities that are not elementally imbued.

All characters can potentially deal Physical damage regardless of their elemental affinity. Historical documentation specifically establishes that Physical does not participate in the standard reaction system.
Physical does not apply an Elemental Aura and does not trigger the Reaction Matrix by itself.
Each element needs its own mechanical fantasy. It is not enough for one to be blue and another red. The correct question is:
What kind of problem can I solve with this element that another element would not solve in exactly the same way?
Many of its historical reactions create zones or physical changes, including Electrified Zone, Swamp, Hurricane, and Quicksand.
Historical reactions include Scald, Magma, Burn, and Withered Zone.
Ice sacrifices offensive speed in exchange for controlling the pace of an encounter.
Electro turns accumulation and proximity into chains of effects.
Plant builds situations that become more important over time.
Wind decides where the fight takes place.
Earth turns the environment into a defensive or offensive tool.
This section begins converting the historical matrix into a system that can function in real-time combat.
An elemental ability may apply an Elemental Aura to:
Example: Suki applies Ice to an enemy. The target is temporarily marked with an Ice Aura.
When a different element comes into contact with the existing Aura:
The first element defines the initial state. The second acts as the Trigger.
This is especially important because the historical matrix already includes reactions whose outcome depends on application order.
Fire → Ice = Weakness    |    Ice → Fire = Melt
Both combinations explicitly appear as different results in the original matrix.
Applying the same element again does NOT generate a reaction.
Historical documentation does not define an exact duration. For the Core Prototype, the following is proposed:
It may be modified depending on:
Specific values must be validated through playtesting. A weak application may last less time, while a specialized application may last longer.
Transform the Aura into another state.
Transform the interaction into an object or zone in the environment.
This is consistent with the original concept of Creations, described as reactions that modify the map.
To avoid a system that becomes impossible to read in real-time combat, a target will initially maintain only one primary Standard Elemental Aura.
Pure Powers may exist as additional markers because they do not necessarily replace the standard element.
Ice Aura + Chaos Mark can coexist.
If several applications arrive almost simultaneously:
The real impact order is used.
The first valid application creates the Aura.
The next compatible application triggers the reaction.
The system never resolves the order randomly.
This ensures that the same input sequence always produces the same result.
The character who applies the second element will initially be considered the Reaction Trigger.
Therefore, that character's statistics will be the primary reference used to calculate the result.
The Alchemy statistic, already present in the documentation, may affect:
The original documentation specifically defines Alchemy as a statistic that amplifies different functions of elemental reactions.
The following table recovers the historical reaction matrix directly from the 2023 document while normalizing several names that appeared with spelling inconsistencies.
Row = element applied first. Column = element applied second.
The original matrix explicitly demonstrates that reaction order is not always symmetrical.
The names below come from the historical source, while several detailed functions are new design proposals because the original material does not fully define what every reaction does.
Water is heated violently, dealing immediate damage and applying a brief scalding effect.
Temporarily immobilizes normal enemies. Against bosses, it contributes to a freeze/stagger meter instead of fully immobilizing them.
Creates a conductive zone that deals periodic Electro pulses while active.
Creates wet, plant-filled terrain that slows movement and favors certain Plant/Water abilities.
Creates a persistent vortex that pulls enemies and distributes Water.
Creates a zone that reduces mobility. Remaining inside too long may cause partial immobilization.
Thermal contrast leaves the target exposed. Proposed effect: temporarily increases damage or stagger received.
Violently discharges accumulated elemental energy. It may deal damage and interrupt actions.
Produces burning roots that restrain targets, deal periodic damage, and may spread across vegetation.
A hot current dries the area. It may deal persistent damage, reduce healing, and weaken existing Plant effects.
Creates a magma surface that deals high persistent damage.
Unlike Weakness, preparing Ice first and applying Fire afterward creates an explosive damage window.
Destabilizes conventional elemental defenses, making the target more susceptible to Pure Powers for a short period.
Progressively reduces mobility and deals light periodic Ice damage.
Reduces movement speed and attack speed.
Ice + Earth creates a temporary physical structure capable of blocking attacks, creating cover, and separating enemies. This takes particular advantage of 3D combat spaces.
Electro energy travels through roots or vegetation, producing pulses between connected enemies.
Creates an area in which Electro discharges strike periodically.
Electro + Earth produces no conventional elemental reaction. Earth discharges or neutralizes the electricity, preserving the original Null cell in the historical matrix.
Plant prepared first and then hydrated grows rapidly. It may create roots or interaction resources.
Frozen plant matter becomes brittle. It may increase stagger, Physical damage, or the ability to break defenses.
Plant + Wind releases spores or particles that may spread the Plant Aura, temporarily increase Alchemy, or prepare new reactions.
Earth provides structure for Plant growth, generating plant elements usable in combat or exploration.
Unlike Hurricane, which may persist, Typhoon produces a fast and violent displacement that may pull enemies inward and then throw them outward.
Wind carries Fire in a direction, allowing flames, Burn, or hot zones to spread.
Wind + Earth creates dust or particles that may reduce enemy accuracy, limit targeting, and enable repositioning.
Pure Powers operate as modifiers to elemental rules rather than conventional members of the 7×7 matrix.
Reduces the target's resistance to the element currently present.
This function is directly documented in the historical material.
Chaos should not reduce every resistance simultaneously. Only the resistance corresponding to the affected element should be reduced.
Temporarily increases the effectiveness of the associated element.
Depending on the kit, it may improve:
Historical documentation establishes that Illumination increases the damage produced by elemental magic.
Spectrum stores the applied element inside a sphere or entity. After a duration, it explodes in an area using that stored element.
This derives directly from the historical Spectrum sphere design.
The target receives Seals associated with the element. These deal periodic damage of the stored element.
Time Clock does NOT trigger reactions. Its balance comes from mechanical freedom.
Time Clock should not be able to:
Physical does NOT trigger elemental reactions. However, it may benefit from the results of those reactions.
In this way, Physical does not create reactions but remains connected to the wider strategic system.
The reaction system should encourage experimentation without allowing one combination to become the universal answer.
Initial maximum: 1 primary Standard Elemental Aura per target.
Initial maximum: 1 simultaneous Pure Power Mark, except for specific kits.
States that support stacking must have an explicit limit.
General proposal: 3 standard stacks. Some characters may modify that value.
Not every state needs to stack.
Freeze, immobilization, and similar forms of hard control cannot be chained indefinitely.
Bosses do not normally receive full immobilization. Instead, reactions may contribute to:
However, high resistance should not automatically mean total immunity unless there is a clear mechanical reason.
Immunities should be used sparingly. An immunity must be communicated before or during the encounter.
Example: a creature made entirely of fire may be immune to Burn.
Avoid arbitrary enemies that invalidate half of the player's team without a readable reason.
Persistent reactions should not trigger infinitely due to extremely rapid attacks.
For the prototype, a small Internal Reaction Cooldown may be used per target and reaction family. The exact value must be tested.
The Alchemy statistic may strengthen reactions, but it needs explicit limits.
A single statistic should not be allowed to scale all of these dimensions simultaneously without constraints.
How to Avoid a Dominant Reaction
Each family should solve a different type of problem:
Pure Manipulation: Chaos, Illumination, Spectrum, Seals.
This principle is consistent with the Game Vision, which already establishes that elemental reactions should not be reduced exclusively to damage multipliers.
The system contains many interactions, so readability is as important as balance.
Each element should be recognizable through:
Color should never be the only way to distinguish an element.
Fractured geometry, distortion, shadows that consume edges.
Audio: Low tones, reversed reverberation, fracture.
Audio: Harmonics, soft bells, bright resonance.
Audio: Seal impact, dry hit, ink/metal.
Audio: Altered ticks, reversed audio, brief silences.
When an important reaction occurs, the player should perceive:
A player should not need to open a menu to understand a basic reaction.
A reaction should use its own icon rather than simply combining colors. This also improves accessibility for players with color-vision limitations.
Three feedback levels can be used.
This is especially important because the original documentation intends some reactions to create objects or alter the map, rather than merely produce floating damage numbers above an enemy.
The elements of Symphony of Justice do not exist only to increase damage. They exist to transform enemies, terrain, movement, and combat opportunities.

This preserves one of the most valuable ideas from the original project. The historical matrix did not simply define “Fire + Water = more damage.” It already included concepts such as Swamp, Hurricane, Quicksand, Electrified Zone, Barriers, Germination, and Visual Obstruction. That direction fits particularly well with the real-time Action RPG being consolidated today because reactions can literally change the space in which combat is taking place.
